attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No available multiscale estimate proves that reflected Wilson products with coincident boundary footprints have zero connected finite boundary cumulant. Gauge invariance and locality kill separated-footprint terms, but they do not yet exclude a local pair-dependent hairpin/cusp/contact operator at \(t=0\).
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity for collared observables: for fixed \(a,L,\delta\), \(Q_{a,L,\delta}(c)=\sum\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\ge0\).

Use RG convergence at fixed \(\delta\) to pass \(a\downarrow0,L\uparrow\infty\); closedness of the positive cone gives a valid positive matrix \(N^\delta\ge0\), and subsequential collar compactness gives \(N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^\delta\ge0\).
Compare the collar-limit matrix with the intended uncollared target by \(N=\Gamma\circ M+A\). Diagonal trace continuity plus \(A\ge0\) forces \(A=0\), so the only possible mismatch is multiplicative.
If all logarithmic cross-ratios of \(\Gamma\) vanish, solve \(\Gamma_{ij}=\alpha_i\overline{\alpha_j}\); then \(N=DMD^*\) and \(M=D^{-1}ND^{-*}\ge0\).
Thus the proof reduces to a Yang-Mills boundary OPE estimate: show that connected coincident-footprint Wilson cumulants vanish or are already included as individual one-body normalizations.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix transfer is valid, but the analytic assertion \(K=0\) is unproved for the Wilson-loop sector. Without it, a nonrank-one multiplicative anomaly could preserve positivity of the collar theory while failing the same-theory OS positivity claim for \(M\).

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: boundary cross-ratio obstruction

assumptions: For every \(\delta>0\), cutoff Schwinger forms for \(T_\delta F_i\) are reflection positive and converge in a topology controlling the finite OS matrix entries.
The collar limit admits \(N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) and an intended trace matrix \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\).
Boundary comparison has the form \(N=\Gamma\circ M+A\), where \(\Gamma_{ij}\ne0\) is multiplicative and \(A\) is an additive contact matrix.
Diagonal trace continuity holds: \(A_{ii}=0\) and \(N_{ii}=\Gamma_{ii}M_{ii}\) with \(\Gamma_{ii}>0\).
The additive contact is OS-positive, \(A\ge0\), and the multiplicative anomaly has zero logarithmic cross-ratios on every finite test family.
definitions: source object: finite cutoff/continuum-collar OS matrices \(N^{\delta}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) obtained from regulated reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger forms after fixed-collar RG limits.
target object: uncollared continuum OS matrix \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) on the locked gauge-invariant test algebra, from which the OS Hilbert space and positive Hamiltonian are reconstructed.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via finite reflected quadratic forms and collar-to-plane trace limits.

same-theory condition: \(F_i\) and \(T_\delta F_i\) represent the same preselected renormalized Wilson/composite observable; allowed boundary factors are only individual diagonal congruences already fixed in the observable normalization, never pair-dependent counterterms introduced to force positivity.

equations.label: fixed-collar positivity
equations.latex: Q_\delta(c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j\,S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\ge0
equations.valid_when: The collars have support in positive Euclidean time separated from the reflection plane and the regulated/lattice theory is reflection positive on the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

equations.label: boundary comparison
equations.valid_when: The collar trace has a finite multiplicative Wilson boundary anomaly and a finite additive contact term for the same target observable \(F_i\).

equations.label: additive contact vanishing
equations.valid_when: \(A\) is a positive semidefinite finite OS contact matrix; follows from Cauchy-Schwarz \(|A_{ij}|^2\le A_{ii}A_{jj}\).

equations.label: cross-ratio criterion
equations.valid_when: All \(amma_{ij}\) are nonzero and a consistent logarithm is chosen on the finite connected index graph; phases are absorbed into \(\alpha_i\).

equations.label: positivity transfer by congruence
equations.valid_when: The cross-ratio criterion gives an invertible diagonal congruence and no additive contact remains.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any finite Wilson family with diagonal trace continuity but \(K_{ik;jl}\ne0\), e.g. a pair-dependent hairpin/cusp factor at the reflection plane; then positivity may hold for the collar-renormalized matrix \(N\) while not proving positivity for the intended same-theory matrix \(M\).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates a valid finite-dimensional bridge: it turns the analytic Wilson trace problem into proving zero connected boundary cross-ratio, after which the OS closed-cone passage is purely linear algebra.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let \(F_1,\dots,F_n\) be locked gauge-invariant Wilson/composite observables in the positive-time algebra and \(T_\delta F_i\) mirror-smooth collars avoiding the reflection plane. If the fixed-collar continuum OS matrices have a boundary trace relation \(N_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}\), with diagonal trace continuity, positive additive contact \(A\ge0\), and vanishing logarithmic cross-ratios of the multiplicative anomaly \(K_{ik;jl}=0\), then OS positivity of \(N\) implies OS positivity of the intended target matrix \(M\). Thus the only remaining same-theory obstruction is a nonzero connected coincident-footprint Wilson boundary OPE.

assumptions: A local boundary OPE exists for reflected Wilson products as collars collapse.
Connected boundary cumulants vanish for disjoint footprints by locality.
For coincident footprints, no gauge-invariant boundary operator contributes a pair-dependent finite term after the pre-locked one-body Wilson renormalizations are applied.
definitions: Boundary footprint \(B(F)\): the limiting intersection/tangent data of the collared Wilson support with the reflection plane.
One-body footprint term: a local functional \(u(F)\) contributing \(u(F_i)+\overline{u(F_j)}\) to \(\log\Gamma_{ij}\).
Connected two-body boundary cumulant: the remainder in \(\log\Gamma_{ij}\) depending simultaneously on the reflected loop \(\Theta F_i\) and the positive-time loop \(F_j\).

equations.label: cumulant decomposition
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly exponentiates and the local boundary OPE separates individual footprint counterterms from connected pair terms.

equations.label: cross-ratio as connected cumulant
equations.valid_when: The same one-body terms \(u_i,\overline{u_j}\) are used in all four entries, so they cancel in the logarithmic cross-ratio.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero connected boundary cumulant from a cusp, hairpin, or curvature-contact operator is a concrete falsifier of this reduction.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the analytic target lemma behind the finite-dimensional bridge: it says exactly what Yang-Mills boundary locality must prove to make the OS positivity transfer valid for Wilson loops.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the logarithm of the Wilson boundary anomaly has a local boundary-cumulant expansion whose connected terms touching both OS labels vanish after subtracting individual one-body footprint counterterms, then all multiplicative cross-ratios \(K_{ik;jl}\) vanish on that Wilson core.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a model or perturbative calculation produces nonzero normalized \(K\) for locked Wilson observables, since then the OS bridge cannot prove positivity for the intended theory without changing the algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves a uniform collar boundary OPE theorem with \(C_{ij}^{\mathrm{conn}}=0\) on a dense mirror-smooth Wilson/composite core and RG convergence valid for those reflected probes.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a sharp finite-dimensional theorem and a concrete analytic gap; the next progress is computable rather than terminological.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone passage is reduced to fixed-collar positivity plus a finite-dimensional cross-ratio/congruence transfer at the reflection-plane trace.
dependency_updates.status: valid modulo Wilson boundary trace estimate

dependency_updates.description: The algebra must be locked before collar removal; individual Wilson renormalizations are allowed, but pair-dependent boundary normalizations are not same-theory operations.
Topology must control not only fixed reflected probes but also the uniform collar trace and the boundary OPE coefficients defining \(\Gamma\) and \(K\).

falsifiers: falsifier: a perturbative or constructive computation of two reflected Wilson collars sharing a boundary tangent gives \(K_{12;12}\ne0\) after all one-body Wilson renormalizations are fixed.
falsifier: the RG cutoff-removal topology controls only collars with distance \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane and provides no uniform trace modulus as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

falsifier: positivity is restored only after adding a pair-dependent boundary counterterm \(Z_{ij}\), which is valid for a modified boundary-renormalized algebra but violates the same-theory condition.
falsifier: an additive mixed contact survives with zero diagonal; this would contradict positive-contact compatibility and signal that the assumed OS-positive boundary OPE decomposition is false.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 188 turns the Wilson boundary obstruction into an exact bridge/falsifier pair. Additive contacts are harmless once diagonal trace continuity and positivity are valid; multiplicative anomalies are harmless exactly when their logarithmic cross-ratio vanishes, equivalently when they are only diagonal congruences. Therefore the real Yang-Mills problem is not generic reflection positivity preservation, but proving absence of connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE terms for reflected Wilson products. A nonzero \(K\) is the compact invariant that falsifies the same-theory bridge.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary OPE for two mirror-smooth rectangular Wilson loops whose collars form a reflected hairpin at \(t=0\); subtract individual perimeter/cusp terms and test whether the residual logarithmic cross-ratio \(K_{ik;jl}\) is zero.
